notes: Back goes to the previous album now, the mirror of the skip button. Pressing back on the first song of an album lands on the last song of the album before it, in the same order the skip button walks forward in.

Both directions read the album off the songs themselves. A play restored after the app was reopened - or an update reload, or a widget resume - came back with its queue and not the album, which is why the buttons still wrapped inside the record.
An album played from the grouped album header in All Songs rolls now too. That header hands its songs over without saying they are an album, so both buttons wrapped inside the record there as well.
The album a play belongs to is saved with the play and restored with it, so a queue picked back up on a new launch still knows which record it is.

What the roll refuses it still refuses: a playlist, a mix, a search result or a play-all of the whole library keeps its own order and wraps inside itself, and a queue that two of your albums both claim is left alone rather than guessed at.
Settings - More - Playback - Next album when one ends switches both directions off, and a finished album then wraps inside itself exactly as it always did, with nothing rolling forward or back.
